subject.title: Feature: Global session reset on auth switch

question: Should OpenClaw add a privileged Gateway-level global auth-refresh operation that preserves active session context, and what exact session scope and authorization boundary should it have?
rationale: The feature changes core session and auth semantics across every channel; source evidence identifies no existing global contract, so choosing scope, safety, and compatibility cannot be resolved mechanically.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped Gateway design
options.body: Define an additive admin-only all-active-sessions refresh contract that preserves session context and invalidates only auth-derived bindings.

options.title: Address concrete switch bugs only
options.body: Keep the feature request open but prioritize narrower provider-switch recovery reports without adding a global session operation.

options.title: Decline global lifecycle control
options.body: Retain per-session reset behavior and document provider-switch recovery as an operator workflow.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a scoped Gateway design
recommendation.body: Define an additive admin-only all-active-sessions refresh contract that preserves session context and invalidates only auth-derived bindings.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway session-reset history and the prior maintainer-facing review make this the strongest routing candidate.
